+  runs), MCP leaving running commands behind on shutdown, expand loading
+  whole originals (now `ExpandTo`/`Store.ExpandTo` stream), Windows run
+  stopping only the direct process (now taskkill /T), plain-text 404/405,
+  case-sensitive Bearer, `/runs/` with an empty key, JSON-RPC batches. All
+  fixed with tests; serve also limits concurrent reductions (a slot is taken
+  only after the body is spooled, so slow uploads block nobody) and has read
+  and idle timeouts. A second pass also fixed the forced kill 5 s after a
+  stop hitting a reused PID (single process and Windows), and JSON pointer

+## For coding agents (MCP)
+
+`abbreviatory mcp` is a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)
+server on standard input and output. Add it to the agent's MCP settings, for
+Claude Code with `claude mcp add abbreviatory -- abbreviatory mcp`, or in the
+JSON most agents read:
+
+```json
+{"mcpServers": {"abbreviatory": {"command": "abbreviatory", "args": ["mcp"]}}}
+```
+
+It offers four tools:
+
+| Tool | What it does |
+|---|---|
+| `run` | Runs a command (`["go", "test", "./..."]`), reduces what it prints and compares with the last run: the agent sees new failures and one line when nothing changed, not the whole output |
+| `reduce` | Reduces output the agent already has, as `text` or a file `path` |
+| `expand` | Returns the original lines behind a reference in a report |
+| `history` | Lists the runs of a history |
+
+`run` takes `cwd`, `timeout_seconds` (10 minutes by default; the command and
+what it started are stopped after that), `stdin`, `key` and `no_history`, and
+every tool takes the options of `reduce` (`budget`, `format`, `preserve`,
+`keep`, `full`, `no_store`). The structured result has the counts, the
+changes and the exit status.
+
+## As an HTTP service
+
+```
+abbreviatory serve                       # http://127.0.0.1:7878, this machine only
+abbreviatory serve -addr :7878 -token T  # reachable from others, with a token
+```
+
+```
+curl -s --data-binary @test.json 'localhost:7878/reduce?budget=3000&key=unit'
+curl -s localhost:7878/expand/8923c60bd06d:g1205
+curl -s localhost:7878/runs/unit
+```
+
+| Endpoint | What it does |
+|---|---|
+| `POST /reduce` | The body is the input; the options are query parameters named as the flags (`budget`, `format`, `preserve`, `keep`, `key`, `full`, `no_store`). Returns the JSON of `reduce -json`, or the report alone with `Accept: text/plain` |
+| `GET /expand/{ref}` | What a reference points to |
+| `GET /runs`, `GET /runs/{key}` | The histories, or one history's runs |
+| `GET /healthz` | `{"status": "ok", "version": ...}`, without the token |
+
+It listens on this machine only unless it has a token (`-token` or
+`$ABBREVIATORY_TOKEN`), and with one it asks every request for it as
+`Authorization: Bearer TOKEN`. Without a token it also refuses requests a web
+page in your browser could send it (other host names, foreign origins), so a
+site you visit can't read your stored logs through it. Errors come back as JSON with a status: 400
+for a bad option or reference, 401 without the token, 403 for a request from
+a web page, 404 for a reference or history not in the store, 413 past `-max-body` (1 GB), 422 for input it
+can't read (binary data, broken JSON with `format=json`).
+
+The command line, the MCP server and the HTTP service share one core, and a
+test checks that they give the same reports, expansions and histories on
+every fixture.
+

diff --git a/cmd/abbreviatory-wasm/main.go b/cmd/abbreviatory-wasm/main.go
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..e46051c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/cmd/abbreviatory-wasm/main.go
@@ -0,0 +1,186 @@
+//go:build js && wasm
+
+// Command abbreviatory-wasm is the engine compiled to WebAssembly for the
+// demo at abbreviatory.com/demo/. It runs in the visitor's browser: inputs
+// are reduced there, kept there for expanding references, and compared with
+// earlier runs there. Nothing is sent anywhere.
+//
+// It sets a global object, abbreviatory, with:
+//
+//	reduce(text, options) -> JSON string: the result as reduce -json gives it
+//	expand(ref)           -> the original text, or throws
+//	forget()              -> drops kept inputs and histories
+//	version               -> the engine version
+//
+// options is a JSON string with format, budget, preserve, keep (an array),
+// key and full, as the command line's flags.
+package main
+
+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"errors"
+	"regexp"
+	"strings"
+	"syscall/js"
+	"time"
+
+	abbreviatory "github.com/abbreviatory/engine"
+)
+
+type kept struct {
+	data  []byte
+	index *abbreviatory.Index
+}
+
+var (
+	originals = map[string]kept{}
+	histories = map[string][]abbreviatory.Run{}
+)
+
+// maxKept is how many inputs are kept for expanding; the oldest go first.
+const maxKept = 20
+
+var order []string
+
+type options struct {
+	Format   string   `json:"format"`
+	Budget   int      `json:"budget"`
+	Preserve *string  `json:"preserve"`
+	Keep     []string `json:"keep"`
+	Key      string   `json:"key"`
+	Full     bool     `json:"full"`
+}
+
+func reduce(text string, raw string) (map[string]any, error) {
+	var o options
+	if raw != "" {
+		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(raw), &o); err != nil {
+			return nil, err
+		}
+	}
+	opt := abbreviatory.Options{Format: o.Format, Budget: o.Budget, Full: o.Full}
+	if opt.Format == "" {
+		opt.Format = "auto"
+	}
+	if err := abbreviatory.CheckFormat(opt.Format); err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	if o.Preserve != nil {
+		opt.Preserve = []string{}
+		for _, p := range strings.Split(*o.Preserve, ",") {
+			if p = strings.TrimSpace(p); p != "" {
+				opt.Preserve = append(opt.Preserve, p)
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	for _, k := range o.Keep {
+		if k == "" {
+			continue
+		}
+		re, err := regexp.Compile(k)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, errors.New("keep: " + err.Error())
+		}
+		opt.Keep = append(opt.Keep, re)
+	}
+	if o.Key != "" {
+		opt.Track = true
+		opt.History = histories[o.Key]
+	}
+	data := []byte(text)
+	start := time.Now()
+	res, err := abbreviatory.Reduce(strings.NewReader(text), opt)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	took := time.Since(start)
+	if _, ok := originals[res.ID]; !ok {
+		order = append(order, res.ID)
+		if len(order) > maxKept {
+			delete(originals, order[0])
+			order = order[1:]
+		}
+	}
+	originals[res.ID] = kept{data, res.Index}
+	out := map[string]any{
+		"version":     abbreviatory.Version,
+		"format":      res.Format,
+		"family":      res.Family,
+		"ref":         res.ID,
+		"input_bytes": res.InputBytes,
+		"input_lines": res.InputLines,
+		"overflow":    res.Overflow,
+		"records":     res.Records,
+		"lines":       res.Lines,
+		"text":        res.Text,
+		"ms":          float64(took.Microseconds()) / 1000,
+	}
+	if res.Run != nil {
+		res.Run.Time = time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339)
+		h := append(histories[o.Key], *res.Run)
+		if len(h) > abbreviatory.FlakyWindow {
+			h[len(h)-abbreviatory.FlakyWindow-1].Trim()
+		}
+		histories[o.Key] = h
+		out["run"] = res.Run.N
+		out["unchanged"] = res.Delta.Unchanged
+		out["new"] = len(res.Delta.New)
+		out["fixed"] = len(res.Delta.Fixed)
+	}
+	return out, nil
+}
+
+func expand(ref string) ([]byte, error) {
+	id, sel, err := abbreviatory.ParseRef(ref)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	k, ok := originals[id]
+	if !ok {
+		return nil, errors.New(id + " is no longer kept in this page; reduce the input again")
+	}
+	return abbreviatory.Expand(k.data, k.index, sel)
+}
+
+func throw(err error) any {
+	return js.Global().Get("Error").New(err.Error())
+}
+
+func main() {
+	api := js.Global().Get("Object").New()
+	api.Set("version", abbreviatory.Version)
+	api.Set("reduce", js.FuncOf(func(this js.Value, args []js.Value) any {
+		if len(args) < 1 {
+			return throw(errors.New("reduce(text, options)"))
+		}
+		opts := ""
+		if len(args) > 1 && args[1].Type() == js.TypeString {
+			opts = args[1].String()
+		}
+		out, err := reduce(args[0].String(), opts)
+		if err != nil {
+			return map[string]any{"error": err.Error()}
+		}
+		b, _ := json.Marshal(out)
+		return string(b)
+	}))
+	api.Set("expand", js.FuncOf(func(this js.Value, args []js.Value) any {
+		if len(args) < 1 {
+			return map[string]any{"error": "expand(ref)"}
+		}
+		data, err := expand(args[0].String())
+		if err != nil {
+			return map[string]any{"error": err.Error()}
+		}
+		return string(data)
+	}))
+	api.Set("forget", js.FuncOf(func(this js.Value, args []js.Value) any {
+		originals, histories, order = map[string]kept{}, map[string][]abbreviatory.Run{}, nil
+		return nil
+	}))
+	js.Global().Set("abbreviatory", api)
+	if cb := js.Global().Get("abbreviatoryReady"); cb.Type() == js.TypeFunction {
+		cb.Invoke()
+	}
+	select {}
+}
diff --git a/cmd/abbreviatory/core.go b/cmd/abbreviatory/core.go
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..c2dedb7
--- /dev/null
+++ b/cmd/abbreviatory/core.go
@@ -0,0 +1,694 @@
+package main
+
+// The core every front end shares: the command line, the HTTP service and
+// the MCP server all reduce, expand, list histories and run commands through
+// these functions, so they give the same results.
+
+import (
+	"errors"
+	"fmt"
+	"io"
+	"io/fs"
+	"os"
+	"os/exec"
+	"os/signal"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"regexp"
+	"runtime"
+	"strconv"
+	"strings"
+	"sync/atomic"
+	"syscall"
+	"time"
+
+	abbreviatory "github.com/abbreviatory/engine"
+	"github.com/abbreviatory/engine/store"
+)
+
+// request is one reduction, however it was asked for.
+type request struct {
+	Format   string
+	Budget   int
+	Preserve *string // nil means "errors,failures,warnings"; "" means nothing
+	Keep     []string
+	NoStore  bool
+	Full     bool
+	Key      string // a history to compare with and record in
+	Command  string // the command that printed the input, when known
+	Exit     *int   // its exit status
+}
+
+// usageError is a mistake in the request itself: the command line exits 2,
+// the HTTP service answers 400, the MCP server returns a tool result marked
+// as an error.
+type usageError struct{ msg string }
+
+func (e *usageError) Error() string { return e.msg }
+
+func usagef(format string, a ...any) error { return &usageError{fmt.Sprintf(format, a...)} }
+
+// options checks the request and turns it into reduce options.
+func (q request) options() (abbreviatory.Options, error) {
+	if q.Format == "" {
+		q.Format = "auto"
+	}
+	if q.Budget == 0 {
+		q.Budget = abbreviatory.DefaultBudget
+	}
+	if q.Budget < abbreviatory.MinBudget {
+		return abbreviatory.Options{}, usagef("budget must be at least %d bytes", abbreviatory.MinBudget)
+	}
+	if err := abbreviatory.CheckFormat(q.Format); err != nil {
+		return abbreviatory.Options{}, &usageError{err.Error()}
+	}
+	opt := abbreviatory.Options{Format: q.Format, Budget: q.Budget, NoRefs: q.NoStore, Full: q.Full, Command: q.Command, Exit: q.Exit}
+	preserve := "errors,failures,warnings"
+	if q.Preserve != nil {
+		preserve = *q.Preserve
+	}
+	opt.Preserve = []string{}
+	for _, p := range strings.Split(preserve, ",") {
+		if p = strings.TrimSpace(p); p != "" {
+			opt.Preserve = append(opt.Preserve, p)
+		}
+	}
+	if err := abbreviatory.CheckPreserve(opt.Preserve); err != nil {
+		return opt, &usageError{err.Error()}
+	}
+	for _, k := range q.Keep {
+		re, err := regexp.Compile(k)
+		if err != nil {
+			return opt, usagef("keep: %v", err)
+		}
+		opt.Keep = append(opt.Keep, re)
+	}
+	return opt, nil
+}
+
+// outcome is a finished reduction with what went wrong on the side.
+type outcome struct {
+	Res      *abbreviatory.Result
+	NoStore  bool
+	Exit     *int
+	Warnings []string
+}
+
+// JSON is the reduction as every front end reports it in JSON.
+func (o *outcome) JSON() map[string]any {
+	res := o.Res
+	out := map[string]any{
+		"version":     abbreviatory.Version,
+		"format":      res.Format,
+		"family":      res.Family,
+		"input_bytes": res.InputBytes,
+		"input_lines": res.InputLines,
+		"overflow":    res.Overflow,
+		"records":     res.Records,
+		"lines":       res.Lines,
+		"text":        res.Text,
+	}
+	if !o.NoStore {
+		out["ref"] = res.ID
+	}
+	if res.Delta != nil {
+		out["run"] = res.Run.N
+		out["delta"] = deltaJSON(res.Delta)
+	}
+	if o.Exit != nil {
+		out["exit"] = *o.Exit
+	}
+	if len(o.Warnings) > 0 {
+		out["warnings"] = o.Warnings
+	}
+	return out
+}
+
+func deltaJSON(d *abbreviatory.Delta) map[string]any {
+	items := func(list []abbreviatory.DeltaItem) []map[string]any {
+		out := []map[string]any{}
+		for _, it := range list {
+			m := map[string]any{"head": it.Head, "ref": it.Ref}
+			if it.Flips > 0 {
+				m["now"], m["changes"], m["window"] = it.Now, it.Flips, it.Window
+			}
+			out = append(out, m)
+		}
+		return out
+	}
+	return map[string]any{
+		"since":     d.Since,
+		"identical": d.Identical,
+		"unchanged": d.Unchanged,
+		"failing":   d.Failing,
+		"new":       items(d.New),
+		"fixed":     items(d.Fixed),
+		"not_run":   items(d.NotRun),
+		"flaky":     items(d.Flaky),
+		"still":     d.Still,
+		"longest":   d.Longest,
+	}
+}
+
+// core holds where the store is.
+type core struct {
+	dir string // the store directory; empty for the default
+}
+
+func (c core) store() (*store.Store, error) {
+	dir := c.dir
+	if dir == "" {
+		d, err := store.DefaultDir()
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, err
+		}
+		dir = d
+	}
+	return store.Open(dir)
+}
+
+// reduce reduces in, storing the original and recording the run in the
+// history when asked. Closing cancel stops a wait for the history's lock;
+// the report is then made without a comparison.
+func (c core) reduce(in io.Reader, q request, cancel <-chan struct{}) (*outcome, error) {
+	opt, err := q.options()
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	o := &outcome{NoStore: q.NoStore, Exit: q.Exit}
+	var st *store.Store
+	if !q.NoStore || q.Key != "" {
+		if st, err = c.store(); err != nil {
+			return nil, err
+		}
+	}
+	if q.Key != "" && !isRegularFile(in) {
+		// With a history the lock is held from reading the history to
+		// writing this run. Read streamed input to a file first, so the
+		// lock isn't held while whatever writes the stream still runs.
+		sp, err := spoolInput(in)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, err
+		}
+		defer os.Remove(sp.Name())
+		defer sp.Close()
+		in = sp
+	}
+	var pend *store.Pending
+	if !q.NoStore {
+		if pend, err = st.Begin(); err != nil {
+			return nil, err
+		}
+		opt.Sink = pend
+	}
+	reduce := func() error {
+		res, err := abbreviatory.Reduce(in, opt)
+		if err != nil {
+			if pend != nil {
+				pend.Abort()
+			}
+			return err
+		}
+		o.Res = res
+		if pend != nil {
+			if err := pend.Commit(res.Index); err != nil {
+				// The report is still worth having; say its references
+				// won't expand.
+				o.Warnings = append(o.Warnings, "the original could not be stored, so the references in this report can't be expanded: "+err.Error())
+			}
+		}
+		return nil
+	}
+	if q.Key == "" {
+		if err := reduce(); err != nil {
+			return nil, err
+		}
+	} else {
+		// Compare and record under the history's lock, so a run of the
+		// same key at the same time waits and then compares with this one.
+		var reduceErr error
+		err := st.UpdateCancel(q.Key, cancel, func(h *store.History) (*abbreviatory.Run, error) {
+			opt.Track = true
+			opt.History = h.Runs
+			if reduceErr = reduce(); reduceErr != nil {
+				return nil, nil
+			}
+			o.Res.Run.Time = time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339)
+			return o.Res.Run, nil
+		})
+		if reduceErr != nil {
+			return nil, reduceErr
+		}
+		if err != nil {
+			if o.Res == nil {
+				// The history couldn't be locked or read: report without it.
+				o.Warnings = append(o.Warnings, "no comparison with the last run: "+err.Error())
+				opt.Track, opt.History = false, nil
+				if err := reduce(); err != nil {
+					return nil, err
+				}
+			} else {
+				o.Warnings = append(o.Warnings, "this run could not be added to the history: "+err.Error())
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	if st != nil {
+		st.PruneNow()
+	}
+	return o, nil
+}
+
+func isRegularFile(r io.Reader) bool {
+	f, ok := r.(*os.File)
+	if !ok {
+		return false
+	}
+	info, err := f.Stat()
+	return err == nil && info.Mode().IsRegular()
+}
+
+// spoolInput copies in to a temporary file and returns it, rewound.
+func spoolInput(in io.Reader) (*os.File, error) {
+	sp, err := os.CreateTemp("", "abbreviatory-in-*")
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	if _, err := io.Copy(sp, in); err != nil {
+		sp.Close()
+		os.Remove(sp.Name())
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	if _, err := sp.Seek(0, io.SeekStart); err != nil {
+		sp.Close()
+		os.Remove(sp.Name())
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	return sp, nil
+}
+
+// expand writes what a reference points to, streamed from the store.
+func (c core) expand(w io.Writer, ref string) error {
+	st, err := c.store()
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	return st.ExpandTo(w, ref)
+}
+
+// errTooLarge is returned by a limitWriter past its limit.
+var errTooLarge = errors.New("too large")
+
+// limitWriter buffers at most n bytes.
+type limitWriter struct {
+	buf []byte
+	n   int
+}
+
+func (l *limitWriter) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
+	if len(l.buf)+len(p) > l.n {
+		return 0, errTooLarge
+	}
+	l.buf = append(l.buf, p...)
+	return len(p), nil
+}
+
+// errNoHistory is returned when no history matches a key.
+var errNoHistory = errors.New("no history matches")
+
+// histories lists every history, most recently run first.
+func (c core) histories() ([]*store.History, error) {
+	st, err := c.store()
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	return st.Histories()
+}
+
+// history finds the history whose key is key or, failing that, the one key
+// that contains key.
+func (c core) history(key string) (*store.History, error) {
+	all, err := c.histories()
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	var match *store.History
+	var matches []string
+	for _, h := range all {
+		if h.Key == key {
+			return h, nil
+		}
+		if strings.Contains(h.Key, key) {
+			match = h
+			matches = append(matches, h.Key)
+		}
+	}
+	if len(matches) > 1 {
+		return nil, usagef("%q matches %d histories:\n  %s", key, len(matches), strings.Join(matches, "\n  "))
+	}
+	if match == nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w %q", errNoHistory, key)
+	}
+	return match, nil
+}
+
+func historiesJSON(all []*store.History) []map[string]any {
+	list := []map[string]any{}
+	for _, h := range all {
+		m := map[string]any{"key": h.Key, "runs": len(h.Runs)}
+		if l := h.Last(); l != nil {
+			m["last"], m["time"], m["failing"] = l.N, l.Time, l.Failing
+		}
+		list = append(list, m)
+	}
+	return list
+}
+
+func historiesText(all []*store.History) string {
+	if len(all) == 0 {
+		return "no histories yet; use reduce -key NAME or run -- COMMAND\n"
+	}
+	var b strings.Builder
+	for _, h := range all {
+		if l := h.Last(); l != nil {
+			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s\n    run %d, %s, %s\n", h.Key, l.N, showTime(l.Time), failingWord(l.Failing))
+		}
+	}
+	return b.String()
+}
+
+func historyJSON(h *store.History) map[string]any {
+	runs := []map[string]any{}
+	for _, r := range h.Runs {
+		m := map[string]any{"run": r.N, "time": r.Time, "ref": r.ID, "format": r.Format, "failing": r.Failing, "new": r.New, "fixed": r.Fixed, "records": r.Records}
+		if r.Exit != nil {
+			m["exit"] = *r.Exit
+		}
+		runs = append(runs, m)
+	}
+	return map[string]any{"key": h.Key, "runs": runs}
+}
+
+func historyText(h *store.History) string {
+	var b strings.Builder
+	b.WriteString(h.Key + "\n")
+	for i := len(h.Runs) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
+		r := h.Runs[i]
+		line := fmt.Sprintf("run %d  %s  %s", r.N, showTime(r.Time), failingWord(r.Failing))
+		var changes []string
+		if r.New > 0 {
+			changes = append(changes, fmt.Sprintf("%d new", r.New))
+		}
+		if r.Fixed > 0 {
+			changes = append(changes, fmt.Sprintf("%d fixed", r.Fixed))
+		}
+		if len(changes) > 0 {
+			line += " (" + strings.Join(changes, ", ") + ")"
+		}
+		if r.Exit != nil {
+			line += fmt.Sprintf("  exit %d", *r.Exit)
+		}
+		b.WriteString(line + "  ref " + r.ID + "\n")
+	}
+	return b.String()
+}
+
+func failingWord(n int) string {
+	switch n {
+	case 0:
+		return "nothing failing"
+	case 1:
+		return "1 failing"
+	}
+	return strconv.Itoa(n) + " failing"
+}
+
+func showTime(s string) string {
+	t, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, s)
+	if err != nil {
+		return "(no time)"
+	}
+	return t.UTC().Format("2006-01-02 15:04 UTC")
+}
+
+// execOpts say how to run a command.
+type execOpts struct {
+	Dir     string
+	Stdin   io.Reader
+	Timeout time.Duration // 0 for none
+	// Forward passes stop signals sent to this process on to the command
+	// (the command line); the MCP server leaves them alone.
+	Forward bool
+	// Cancel, when closed, stops the command (an MCP client cancelled).
+	Cancel <-chan struct{}
+	// Group starts the command in a process group of its own, and a
+	// timeout or a cancel stops the whole group (the MCP server, where no
+	// terminal is involved).
+	Group bool
+}
+
+// executed is a command that ran: its status and its output, spooled.
+type executed struct {
+	Status   int
+	Output   io.Reader
+	Warnings []string
+	spool    *os.File
+	extra    io.Closer
+}
+
+// Close removes the spooled output.
+func (e *executed) Close() {
+	if e.extra != nil {
+		e.extra.Close()
+	}
+	if e.spool != nil {
+		e.spool.Close()
+		os.Remove(e.spool.Name())
+	}
+}
+
+// startError is a command that couldn't be started; Status is 127 when it
+// wasn't found, else 126.
+type startError struct {
+	Status int
+	Err    error
+	Name   string
+}
+
+func (e *startError) Error() string { return "cannot run " + e.Name + ": " + e.Err.Error() }
+
+// execute runs argv with standard output and standard error going into one
+// pipe, spools what it prints to disk (memory stays flat; the exit status is
+// only known at the end) and returns it with the exit status.
+func execute(argv []string, x execOpts) (*executed, error) {
+	r, w, err := os.Pipe()
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	cmd := exec.Command(argv[0], argv[1:]...)
+	cmd.Dir = x.Dir
+	cmd.Stdin = x.Stdin
+	cmd.Stdout = w
+	cmd.Stderr = w
+	if x.Group {
+		ownGroup(cmd)
+	}
+	if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
+		w.Close()
+		r.Close()
+		status := 126
+		if errors.Is(err, exec.ErrNotFound) || errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
+			status = 127
+		}
+		return nil, &startError{Status: status, Err: err, Name: argv[0]}
+	}
+	w.Close()
+
+	var forwarded chan struct{}
+	var sigs chan os.Signal
+	if x.Forward {
+		// A signal meant to stop the job (a CI timeout or cancel, Ctrl-C)
+		// is passed on to the command; the report is still made from what
+		// it printed. A second one kills it.
+		sigs = make(chan os.Signal, 2)
+		signal.Notify(sigs, stopSignals...)
+		forwarded = make(chan struct{})
+		go func() {
+			defer close(forwarded)
+			n := 0
+			for sig := range sigs {
+				if n++; n == 1 && cmd.Process.Signal(sig) == nil {
+					continue
+				}
+				cmd.Process.Kill()
+			}
+		}()
+	}
+	// The second, forceful step of stopping a single process is skipped once
+	// it has exited: its process ID may already belong to something else.
+	var exited atomic.Bool
+	stop := func() {
+		if x.Group {
+			if stopGroup(cmd, false) != nil {
+				stopGroup(cmd, true)
+				return
+			}
+			if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
+				return // taskkill /F has ended the tree already
+			}
+			// The group's ID stays taken while any of it runs, so this also
+			// reaches what the command left behind ignoring SIGTERM.
+			time.AfterFunc(5*time.Second, func() { stopGroup(cmd, true) })
+			return
+		}
+		if cmd.Process.Signal(os.Interrupt) != nil {
+			cmd.Process.Kill()
+			return
+		}
+		time.AfterFunc(5*time.Second, func() {
+			if !exited.Load() {
+				cmd.Process.Kill()
+			}
+		})
+	}
+	if x.Cancel != nil {
+		finished := make(chan struct{})
+		defer close(finished)
+		go func() {
+			select {
+			case <-x.Cancel:
+				stop()
+			case <-finished:
+			}
+		}()
+	}
+	var timedOut atomic.Bool
+	if x.Timeout > 0 {
+		t := time.AfterFunc(x.Timeout, func() {
+			timedOut.Store(true)
+			stop()
+		})
+		defer t.Stop()
+	}
+
+	e := &executed{}
+	spool, err := os.CreateTemp("", "abbreviatory-run-*")
+	if err != nil {
+		io.Copy(io.Discard, r)
+		cmd.Wait()
+		if x.Forward {
+			signal.Stop(sigs)
+			close(sigs)
+			<-forwarded
+		}
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	e.spool = spool
+	var written atomic.Int64
+	copied := make(chan error, 1)
+	go func() {
+		_, err := io.Copy(countingWriter{spool, &written}, r)
+		copied <- err
+	}()
+	waitErr := cmd.Wait()
+	exited.Store(true)
+	e.Status = exitOf(cmd, 1)
+	if x.Forward {
+		signal.Stop(sigs)
+		close(sigs)
+		<-forwarded
+	}
+	if waitErr != nil && cmd.ProcessState == nil {
+		e.Warnings = append(e.Warnings, waitErr.Error())
+	}
+	if timedOut.Load() {
+		e.Warnings = append(e.Warnings, "the command ran past its time limit of "+x.Timeout.String()+" and was stopped")
+	}
+
+	// Something the command started in the background can keep the output
+	// open after the command is gone; take what came within a grace period
+	// and leave the rest.
+	select {
+	case err := <-copied:
+		r.Close()
+		if err != nil {
+			e.Close()
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("reading the command's output: %w", err)
+		}
+		if _, err := spool.Seek(0, io.SeekStart); err != nil {
+			e.Close()
+			return nil, err
+		}
+		e.Output = spool
+	case <-time.After(outputGrace):
+		e.Warnings = append(e.Warnings, fmt.Sprintf("the output was still open %s after the command exited (a process it started in the background?); reading stopped", outputGrace))
+		rf, err := os.Open(spool.Name())
+		if err != nil {
+			e.Close()
+			return nil, err
+		}
+		e.extra = rf
+		e.Output = io.LimitReader(rf, written.Load())
+	}
+	return e, nil
+}
+
+// countingWriter counts what it writes.
+type countingWriter struct {
+	w io.Writer
+	n *atomic.Int64
+}
+
+func (c countingWriter) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
+	n, err := c.w.Write(p)
+	c.n.Add(int64(n))
+	return n, err
+}
+
+// outputGrace is how long run keeps reading output after the command exits.
+var outputGrace = 5 * time.Second
+
+// stopSignals are the signals run passes on to the command.
+var stopSignals = []os.Signal{os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM}
+
+// exitOf is the command's exit status: its own code, 128 plus the signal
+// number when a signal ended it, or def if it never ran.
+func exitOf(cmd *exec.Cmd, def int) int {
+	ps := cmd.ProcessState
+	if ps == nil {
+		return def
+	}
+	if code := ps.ExitCode(); code >= 0 {
+		return code
+	}
+	if ws, ok := ps.Sys().(syscall.WaitStatus); ok && ws.Signaled() {
+		return 128 + int(ws.Signal())
+	}
+	return def
+}
+
+// defaultKey names the history of a command: the project it runs in (the
+// enclosing Git repository, or dir itself) and the command.
+func defaultKey(dir, command string) string {
+	if dir == "" {
+		d, err := os.Getwd()
+		if err != nil {
+			return command
+		}
+		dir = d
+	}
+	if abs, err := filepath.Abs(dir); err == nil {
+		dir = abs
+	}
+	project := dir
+	for d := dir; ; {
+		if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(d, ".git")); err == nil {
+			project = d
+			break
+		}
+		parent := filepath.Dir(d)
+		if parent == d {
+			break
+		}
+		d = parent
+	}
+	return project + ": " + command
+}

+package main
+
+// abbreviatory mcp: a Model Context Protocol server over standard input and
+// output, for coding agents. It speaks JSON-RPC 2.0, one message per line,
+// and offers four tools: reduce, run, expand and history.
+
+import (
+	"bufio"
+	"bytes"
+	"encoding/json"
+	"errors"
+	"flag"
+	"fmt"
+	"io"
+	"os"
+	"os/signal"
+	"strings"
+	"sync"
+	"time"
+
+	abbreviatory "github.com/abbreviatory/engine"
+)
+
+// mcpVersions are the protocol versions the server speaks, newest first.
+var mcpVersions = []string{"2025-06-18", "2025-03-26", "2024-11-05"}
+
+// Limits for the MCP server.
+const (
+	mcpMaxMessage    = 256 << 20 // the largest message read
+	mcpDefaultExpand = 4 << 20   // what expand returns at most unless asked
+	mcpMaxExpand     = 64 << 20
+	mcpDefaultTime   = 10 * time.Minute
+)
+
+func cmdMCP(args []string, stdin io.Reader, stdout, stderr io.Writer) int {
+	fs := flag.NewFlagSet("mcp", flag.ContinueOnError)
+	fs.SetOutput(stderr)
+	dir := storeFlag(fs)
+	fs.Usage = func() {
+		fmt.Fprint(stderr, "Usage: abbreviatory mcp [flags]\n\nServes the tools reduce, run, expand and history to a coding agent over\nthe Model Context Protocol on standard input and output. Add it to the\nagent's MCP settings as the command \"abbreviatory mcp\".\n\n")
+		fs.PrintDefaults()
+	}
+	if err := fs.Parse(args); err != nil {
+		if errors.Is(err, flag.ErrHelp) {
+			return 0
+		}
+		return 2
+	}
+	if fs.NArg() > 0 {
+		fs.Usage()
+		return 2
+	}
+	s := &mcpServer{c: core{*dir}, out: stdout, running: map[string]*mcpCall{}}
+	// Stopped by a signal (a client shutting the server down): stop the
+	// commands still running, with what they started, before going.
+	sigs := make(chan os.Signal, 1)
+	signal.Notify(sigs, stopSignals...)
+	defer signal.Stop(sigs)
+	go func() {
+		if _, ok := <-sigs; ok {
+			s.shutdown()
+			os.Exit(0)
+		}
+	}()
+	if err := s.serve(stdin); err != nil {
+		fmt.Fprintln(stderr, "abbreviatory:", err)
+		return 1
+	}
+	return 0
+}
+
+type mcpServer struct {
+	c       core
+	out     io.Writer
+	mu      sync.Mutex // guards out and running
+	running map[string]*mcpCall
+	wg      sync.WaitGroup
+}
+
+// mcpCall is a tools/call in progress. Closing stop stops its command; a
+// call the client cancelled gets no answer, one stopped because the server
+// is stopping still does.
+type mcpCall struct {
+	stop      chan struct{}
+	stopped   bool
+	cancelled bool
+}
+
+func (c *mcpCall) halt() {
+	if !c.stopped {
+		c.stopped = true
+		close(c.stop)
+	}
+}
+
+type rpcMessage struct {
+	JSONRPC string          `json:"jsonrpc"`
+	ID      json.RawMessage `json:"id,omitempty"`
+	Method  string          `json:"method,omitempty"`
+	Params  json.RawMessage `json:"params,omitempty"`
+}
+
+type rpcError struct {
+	Code    int    `json:"code"`
+	Message string `json:"message"`
+}
+
+// serve reads messages until the input ends. Each request is answered in its
+// own goroutine, so a long run doesn't hold up a ping or a cancellation. When
+// the input ends the client is gone: running commands are stopped.
+func (s *mcpServer) serve(in io.Reader) error {
+	r := bufio.NewReaderSize(in, 1<<20)
+	defer s.shutdown()
+	for {
+		line, err := readMessage(r)
+		if len(bytes.TrimSpace(line)) > 0 {
+			s.handle(line)
+		}
+		if err == io.EOF {
+			return nil
+		}
+		if err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+// shutdown stops every running command (SIGTERM to its process group, then
+// SIGKILL after 5 seconds) and waits for them, at most 8 seconds.
+func (s *mcpServer) shutdown() {
+	s.mu.Lock()
+	for _, c := range s.running {
+		c.halt()
+	}
+	s.mu.Unlock()
+	done := make(chan struct{})
+	go func() {
+		s.wg.Wait()
+		close(done)
+	}()
+	select {
+	case <-done:
+	case <-time.After(8 * time.Second):
+	}
+}
+
+func readMessage(r *bufio.Reader) ([]byte, error) {
+	var buf []byte
+	for {
+		part, err := r.ReadSlice('\n')
+		buf = append(buf, part...)
+		if len(buf) > mcpMaxMessage {
+			// Skip the rest of it.
+			for err == bufio.ErrBufferFull {
+				_, err = r.ReadSlice('\n')
+			}
+			return []byte(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"(too large)"}`), err
+		}
+		if err != bufio.ErrBufferFull {
+			return buf, err
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+func (s *mcpServer) send(v any) {
+	data, err := json.Marshal(v)
+	if err != nil {
+		data, _ = json.Marshal(map[string]any{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "error": rpcError{-32603, err.Error()}})
+	}
+	s.mu.Lock()
+	defer s.mu.Unlock()
+	s.out.Write(append(data, '\n'))
+}
+
+func (s *mcpServer) reply(id json.RawMessage, result any) {
+	s.send(map[string]any{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": id, "result": result})
+}
+
+func (s *mcpServer) fail(id json.RawMessage, code int, msg string) {
+	if id == nil {
+		id = json.RawMessage("null")
+	}
+	s.send(map[string]any{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": id, "error": rpcError{code, msg}})
+}
+
+func (s *mcpServer) handle(line []byte) {
+	if !json.Valid(line) {
+		s.fail(nil, -32700, "parse error: not JSON")
+		return
+	}
+	if t := bytes.TrimSpace(line); t[0] != '{' {
+		// Batches went out of the protocol in 2025-06-18; anything but an
+		// object isn't a request.
+		s.fail(nil, -32600, "invalid request: expected one JSON-RPC object")
+		return
+	}
+	var m rpcMessage
+	if err := json.Unmarshal(line, &m); err != nil {
+		s.fail(nil, -32600, "invalid request: "+err.Error())
+		return
+	}
+	if m.Method == "" {
+		// A response from the client (the server sends no requests), or
+		// nonsense: nothing to answer.
+		return
+	}
+	if m.Method == "(too large)" {
+		s.fail(nil, -32600, fmt.Sprintf("message larger than %d MB", mcpMaxMessage>>20))
+		return
+	}
+	notification := len(m.ID) == 0
+	switch m.Method {
+	case "notifications/initialized", "notifications/roots/list_changed":
+		return
+	case "notifications/cancelled":
+		var p struct {
+			RequestID json.RawMessage `json:"requestId"`
+		}
+		json.Unmarshal(m.Params, &p)
+		s.mu.Lock()
+		if c, ok := s.running[string(p.RequestID)]; ok {
+			c.cancelled = true
+			c.halt()
+		}
+		s.mu.Unlock()
+		return
+	}
+	if notification {
+		return
+	}
+	switch m.Method {
+	case "initialize":
+		var p struct {
+			ProtocolVersion string `json:"protocolVersion"`
+		}
+		json.Unmarshal(m.Params, &p)
+		version := mcpVersions[0]
+		for _, v := range mcpVersions {
+			if v == p.ProtocolVersion {
+				version = v
+			}
+		}
+		s.reply(m.ID, map[string]any{
+			"protocolVersion": version,
+			"capabilities":    map[string]any{"tools": map[string]any{}},
+			"serverInfo":      map[string]any{"name": "abbreviatory", "version": abbreviatory.Version},
+			"instructions":    mcpInstructions,
+		})
+	case "ping":
+		s.reply(m.ID, map[string]any{})
+	case "tools/list":
+		s.reply(m.ID, map[string]any{"tools": mcpTools()})
+	case "tools/call":
+		call := &mcpCall{stop: make(chan struct{})}
+		s.mu.Lock()
+		s.running[string(m.ID)] = call
+		s.mu.Unlock()
+		s.wg.Add(1)
+		go func() {
+			defer s.wg.Done()
+			result, rerr := s.call(m.Params, call.stop)
+			s.mu.Lock()
+			cancelled := call.cancelled
+			if s.running[string(m.ID)] == call {
+				delete(s.running, string(m.ID))
+			}
+			s.mu.Unlock()
+			if cancelled {
+				return // the client cancelled it: no answer is expected
+			}
+			if rerr != nil {
+				s.fail(m.ID, rerr.Code, rerr.Message)
+				return
+			}
+			s.reply(m.ID, result)
+		}()
+	default:
+		s.fail(m.ID, -32601, "unknown method "+m.Method)
+	}
+}
+
+const mcpInstructions = "Abbreviatory reduces large tool output (test runs, build and application logs, JSON) to a short report within a byte budget: failures, errors and warnings first, repeats folded into one line with a count, every left-out part reachable through a reference such as [ref 3f2a9c1b7e04:g12]. Use run to run a test or build command instead of reading its whole output; with a history it says what changed since the last run (new, fixed, still failing, flaky), and one line when nothing did. Use expand on a reference to see the original lines."
+
+// toolArgs are the arguments every tool may get; each uses its own.
+type toolArgs struct {
+	Text      *string  `json:"text"`
+	Path      string   `json:"path"`
+	Command   []string `json:"command"`
+	Cwd       string   `json:"cwd"`
+	Timeout   int      `json:"timeout_seconds"`
+	Ref       string   `json:"ref"`
+	MaxBytes  int      `json:"max_bytes"`
+	Format    string   `json:"format"`
+	Budget    int      `json:"budget"`
+	Preserve  *string  `json:"preserve"`
+	Keep      []string `json:"keep"`
+	Key       string   `json:"key"`
+	Full      bool     `json:"full"`
+	NoStore   bool     `json:"no_store"`
+	NoHistory bool     `json:"no_history"`
+	Stdin     *string  `json:"stdin"`
+}
+
+func (a toolArgs) request() request {
+	return request{Format: a.Format, Budget: a.Budget, Preserve: a.Preserve, Keep: a.Keep, Key: a.Key, Full: a.Full, NoStore: a.NoStore}
+}
+
+// call runs a tool. Problems with the tool's work come back as a result
+// with isError set, as the protocol asks; only an unknown tool or arguments
+// that aren't JSON are protocol errors.
+func (s *mcpServer) call(params json.RawMessage, cancel <-chan struct{}) (any, *rpcError) {
+	var p struct {
+		Name      string          `json:"name"`
+		Arguments json.RawMessage `json:"arguments"`
+	}
+	if err := json.Unmarshal(params, &p); err != nil {
+		return nil, &rpcError{-32602, "invalid params: " + err.Error()}
+	}
+	var a toolArgs
+	if len(p.Arguments) > 0 && string(p.Arguments) != "null" {
+		dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(p.Arguments))
+		dec.DisallowUnknownFields()
+		if err := dec.Decode(&a); err != nil {
+			return toolError("bad arguments for " + p.Name + ": " + err.Error()), nil
+		}
+	}
+	switch p.Name {
+	case "reduce":
+		return s.toolReduce(a, cancel), nil
+	case "run":
+		return s.toolRun(a, cancel), nil
+	case "expand":
+		return s.toolExpand(a), nil
+	case "history":
+		return s.toolHistory(a), nil
+	}
+	return nil, &rpcError{-32602, "unknown tool " + p.Name}
+}
+
+func toolError(msg string) map[string]any {
+	return map[string]any{"content": []map[string]any{{"type": "text", "text": msg}}, "isError": true}
+}
+
+func toolText(text string, structured any) map[string]any {
+	out := map[string]any{"content": []map[string]any{{"type": "text", "text": text}}, "isError": false}
+	if structured != nil {
+		out["structuredContent"] = structured
+	}
+	return out
+}
+
+func (s *mcpServer) toolReduce(a toolArgs, cancel <-chan struct{}) map[string]any {
+	var in io.Reader
+	switch {
+	case a.Text != nil && a.Path != "":
+		return toolError("give text or path, not both")
+	case a.Text != nil:
+		in = strings.NewReader(*a.Text)
+	case a.Path != "":
+		f, err := os.Open(a.Path)
+		if err != nil {
+			return toolError(err.Error())
+		}
+		defer f.Close()
+		in = f
+	default:
+		return toolError("give the output to reduce as text, or a file as path")
+	}
+	o, err := s.c.reduce(in, a.request(), cancel)
+	if err != nil {
+		return toolError(err.Error())
+	}
+	return withWarnings(toolText(o.Res.Text, o.JSON()), o.Warnings)
+}
+
+func (s *mcpServer) toolRun(a toolArgs, cancel <-chan struct{}) map[string]any {
+	if len(a.Command) == 0 {
+		return toolError("give the command as an array, such as [\"go\", \"test\", \"./...\"]")
+	}
+	timeout := mcpDefaultTime
+	if a.Timeout > 0 {
+		timeout = time.Duration(a.Timeout) * time.Second
+	}
+	x := execOpts{Dir: a.Cwd, Timeout: timeout, Cancel: cancel, Group: true}
+	if a.Stdin != nil {
+		x.Stdin = strings.NewReader(*a.Stdin)
+	}
+	e, err := execute(a.Command, x)
+	if err != nil {
+		var se *startError
+		if errors.As(err, &se) {
+			return toolError(fmt.Sprintf("%v (exit status %d)", err, se.Status))
+		}
+		return toolError(err.Error())
+	}
+	defer e.Close()
+	q := a.request()
+	q.Command = strings.Join(a.Command, " ")
+	status := e.Status
+	q.Exit = &status
+	if a.NoHistory {
+		q.Key = ""
+	} else if q.Key == "" {
+		q.Key = defaultKey(a.Cwd, q.Command)
+	}
+	o, err := s.c.reduce(e.Output, q, cancel)
+	if err != nil {
+		return toolError(fmt.Sprintf("the command exited with status %d, and its output could not be reduced: %v", status, err))
+	}
+	o.Warnings = append(e.Warnings, o.Warnings...)
+	result := toolText(o.Res.Text, o.JSON())
+	if a.NoHistory {
+		// Without a history the report doesn't show the exit status.
+		result["content"] = append(result["content"].([]map[string]any), map[string]any{"type": "text", "text": fmt.Sprintf("exit status %d", status)})
+	}
+	return withWarnings(result, o.Warnings)
+}
+
+func withWarnings(result map[string]any, warnings []string) map[string]any {
+	if len(warnings) > 0 {
+		result["content"] = append(result["content"].([]map[string]any), map[string]any{"type": "text", "text": "warning: " + strings.Join(warnings, "\nwarning: ")})
+	}
+	return result
+}
+
+func (s *mcpServer) toolExpand(a toolArgs) map[string]any {
+	if a.Ref == "" {
+		return toolError("give a reference such as 3f2a9c1b7e04:g12")
+	}
+	limit := mcpDefaultExpand
+	if a.MaxBytes > 0 {
+		limit = min(a.MaxBytes, mcpMaxExpand)
+	}
+	lw := &limitWriter{n: limit}
+	if err := s.c.expand(lw, a.Ref); err != nil {
+		if errors.Is(err, errTooLarge) {
+			return toolError(fmt.Sprintf("%s is more than the %d bytes this returns; expand a part of it, such as a group (:g12), a kind (:error) or a line range (:L1-500), or raise max_bytes (up to %d)", a.Ref, limit, mcpMaxExpand))
+		}
+		return toolError(err.Error())
+	}
+	return toolText(string(lw.buf), nil)
+}
+
+func (s *mcpServer) toolHistory(a toolArgs) map[string]any {
+	if a.Key == "" {
+		all, err := s.c.histories()
+		if err != nil {
+			return toolError(err.Error())
+		}
+		return toolText(historiesText(all), map[string]any{"histories": historiesJSON(all)})
+	}
+	h, err := s.c.history(a.Key)
+	if err != nil {
+		return toolError(err.Error())
+	}
+	return toolText(historyText(h), historyJSON(h))
+}
+
+// mcpTools describes the tools for tools/list.
+func mcpTools() []map[string]any {
+	str := func(desc string) map[string]any { return map[string]any{"type": "string", "description": desc} }
+	integer := func(desc string) map[string]any { return map[string]any{"type": "integer", "description": desc} }
+	boolean := func(desc string) map[string]any { return map[string]any{"type": "boolean", "description": desc} }
+	common := func(props map[string]any) map[string]any {
+		props["format"] = str("auto (the default), test-output, logs, json, or one of: " + strings.Join(abbreviatory.FormatNames(), ", "))
+		props["budget"] = integer(fmt.Sprintf("most bytes of the report; default %d, at least %d", abbreviatory.DefaultBudget, abbreviatory.MinBudget))
+		props["preserve"] = str("what is always shown or referenced: any of errors, failures, warnings, comma separated; default all three, empty for none")
+		props["keep"] = map[string]any{"type": "array", "items": map[string]any{"type": "string"}, "description": "regular expressions; matching lines are kept like errors"}
+		props["full"] = boolean("with a history, the whole report even when nothing changed since the last run")
+		props["no_store"] = boolean("don't keep the original; the report then has no references")
+		return props
+	}
+	return []map[string]any{
+		{
+			"name":        "reduce",
+			"title":       "Reduce output",
+			"description": "Reduce tool output (a test run, a build or application log, a JSON document) to a short report: failures, errors and warnings first, repeats folded with a count, within the byte budget. Parts left out carry references for expand. Give key to compare with the last reduction under that key.",
+			"inputSchema": map[string]any{"type": "object", "properties": common(map[string]any{
+				"text": str("the output to reduce"),
+				"path": str("a file to reduce instead of text"),
+				"key":  str("a history name: compare with the last run under it and record this one"),
+			})},
+		},
+		{
+			"name":        "run",
+			"title":       "Run a command and reduce its output",
+			"description": "Run a command (tests, a build, a linter), reduce what it prints (standard output and standard error together) and compare with its last run: new failures, fixed ones, still failing, flaky. One line when nothing changed. The report shows the exit status.",
+			"inputSchema": map[string]any{"type": "object", "required": []string{"command"}, "properties": common(map[string]any{
+				"command":         map[string]any{"type": "array", "items": map[string]any{"type": "string"}, "description": "the command and its arguments, such as [\"go\", \"test\", \"./...\"]; not run through a shell"},
+				"cwd":             str("the directory to run it in; default the server's"),
+				"timeout_seconds": integer("stop the command after this long; default 600"),
+				"stdin":           str("text to give the command on standard input"),
+				"key":             str("the history name; default the project directory and the command"),
+				"no_history":      boolean("don't compare with the last run or record this one"),
+			})},
+		},
+		{
+			"name":        "expand",
+			"title":       "Expand a reference",
+			"description": "Return the original lines a reference from a report points to, byte for byte. References look like 3f2a9c1b7e04:g12 (a group), :error or :fail (every line of a kind), :L10-40 (a line range), or no selector (the whole input).",
+			"inputSchema": map[string]any{"type": "object", "required": []string{"ref"}, "properties": map[string]any{
+				"ref":       str("the reference, with or without the brackets and the word ref"),
+				"max_bytes": integer(fmt.Sprintf("the most bytes to return; default %d, up to %d", mcpDefaultExpand, mcpMaxExpand)),
+			}},
+		},
+		{
+			"name":        "history",
+			"title":       "List run histories",
+			"description": "List the run histories, or with key the runs of one: when, how many failing, how many new and fixed, the exit status and the reference of each.",
+			"inputSchema": map[string]any{"type": "object", "properties": map[string]any{
+				"key": str("the history's key, or a part of it that matches one"),
+			}},
+		},
+	}
+}

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..0bf63a8

+package main
+
+import (
+	"bufio"
+	"encoding/json"
+	"io"
+	"os"
+	"os/exec"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"runtime"
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+	"time"
+)
+
+// mcpSession drives the MCP server over pipes, as an agent would.
+type mcpSession struct {
+	t    *testing.T
+	in   io.WriteCloser
+	out  *bufio.Reader
+	done chan int
+}
+
+func startMCP(t *testing.T, dir string) *mcpSession {
+	inR, inW := io.Pipe()
+	outR, outW := io.Pipe()
+	s := &mcpSession{t: t, in: inW, out: bufio.NewReader(outR), done: make(chan int, 1)}
+	go func() {
+		code := run([]string{"mcp", "-store", dir}, inR, outW, io.Discard)
+		outW.Close()
+		s.done <- code
+	}()
+	t.Cleanup(func() { inW.Close() })
+	return s
+}
+
+func (s *mcpSession) send(msg string) {
+	if _, err := io.WriteString(s.in, msg+"\n"); err != nil {
+		s.t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+}
+
+func (s *mcpSession) recv() map[string]any {
+	type line struct {
+		b   []byte
+		err error
+	}
+	ch := make(chan line, 1)
+	go func() {
+		b, err := s.out.ReadBytes('\n')
+		ch <- line{b, err}
+	}()
+	select {
+	case l := <-ch:
+		if l.err != nil {
+			s.t.Fatalf("reading from the server: %v", l.err)
+		}
+		var m map[string]any
+		if err := json.Unmarshal(l.b, &m); err != nil {
+			s.t.Fatalf("not JSON: %s", l.b)
+		}
+		return m
+	case <-time.After(20 * time.Second):
+		s.t.Fatal("no answer from the server")
+		return nil
+	}
+}
+
+func TestMCPProtocol(t *testing.T) {
+	s := startMCP(t, t.TempDir())
+	s.send(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-03-26","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"test","version":"1"}}}`)
+	m := s.recv()
+	r := m["result"].(map[string]any)
+	if r["protocolVersion"] != "2025-03-26" || r["serverInfo"].(map[string]any)["name"] != "abbreviatory" {
+		t.Fatalf("initialize: %v", m)
+	}
+	s.send(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}`)
+	s.send(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"a","method":"ping"}`)
+	if m := s.recv(); m["id"] != "a" || m["result"] == nil {
+		t.Fatalf("ping: %v", m)
+	}
+	s.send(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}`)
+	tools := s.recv()["result"].(map[string]any)["tools"].([]any)
+	var names []string
+	for _, tl := range tools {
+		tm := tl.(map[string]any)
+		names = append(names, tm["name"].(string))
+		if tm["inputSchema"].(map[string]any)["type"] != "object" || tm["description"] == "" {
+			t.Fatalf("tool %v", tm)
+		}
+	}
+	if strings.Join(names, ",") != "reduce,run,expand,history" {
+		t.Fatalf("tools: %v", names)
+	}
+	// An unknown version gets the newest.
+	s.send(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"1999-01-01"}}`)
+	if v := s.recv()["result"].(map[string]any)["protocolVersion"]; v != mcpVersions[0] {
+		t.Fatalf("version for an unknown one: %v", v)
+	}
+	for _, c := range []struct {
+		msg  string
+		code float64
+	}{
+		{`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":4,"method":"resources/list"}`, -32601},
+		{`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":5,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"frobnicate","arguments":{}}}`, -32602},
+		{`not json`, -32700},
+	} {
+		s.send(c.msg)
+		m := s.recv()
+		if e, ok := m["error"].(map[string]any); !ok || e["code"] != c.code {
+			t.Fatalf("%s: %v", c.msg, m)
+		}
+	}
+	// Tool problems come back as results marked as errors.
+	for _, args := range []string{`{}`, `{"text":"x","path":"y"}`, `{"text":"x","budget":5}`, `{"text":"x","bogus":1}`, `{"path":"/no/such/file"}`} {
+		s.send(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":6,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"reduce","arguments":` + args + `}}`)
+		r := s.recv()["result"].(map[string]any)
+		if r["isError"] != true {
+			t.Fatalf("reduce %s: %v", args, r)
+		}
+	}
+	s.send(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"reduce","arguments":{"text":"2026-10-18T08:00:01Z ERROR disk full\n"}}}`)
+	r = s.recv()["result"].(map[string]any)
+	text := r["content"].([]any)[0].(map[string]any)["text"].(string)
+	if r["isError"] != false || !strings.Contains(text, "ERROR disk full") {
+		t.Fatalf("reduce: %v", r)
+	}
+	ref := r["structuredContent"].(map[string]any)["ref"].(string)
+	s.send(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":8,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"expand","arguments":{"ref":"` + ref + `","max_bytes":10}}}`)
+	if r := s.recv()["result"].(map[string]any); r["isError"] != true || !strings.Contains(r["content"].([]any)[0].(map[string]any)["text"].(string), "raise max_bytes") {
+		t.Fatalf("expand over the limit: %v", r)
+	}
+	s.in.Close()
+	if code := <-s.done; code != 0 {
+		t.Fatalf("exit %d at the end of input", code)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestMCPRun(t *testing.T) {
+	if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
+		t.Skip("uses sh")
+	}
+	dir := t.TempDir()
+	s := startMCP(t, dir)
+	call := func(id, args string) map[string]any {
+		s.send(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":` + id + `,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"run","arguments":` + args + `}}`)
+		return s.recv()["result"].(map[string]any)
+	}
+	texts := func(r map[string]any) []string {
+		var out []string
+		for _, c := range r["content"].([]any) {
+			out = append(out, c.(map[string]any)["text"].(string))
+		}
+		return out
+	}
+	r := call("1", `{"command":["sh","-c","echo x ERROR boom; exit 3"],"key":"job"}`)
+	if r["isError"] != false || !strings.Contains(texts(r)[0], "run 1, exit status 3") || r["structuredContent"].(map[string]any)["exit"] != float64(3) {
+		t.Fatalf("run: %v", r)
+	}
+	r = call("2", `{"command":["sh","-c","echo x ERROR boom; exit 3"],"key":"job"}`)
+	if !strings.Contains(texts(r)[0], "run 2, exit status 3, identical to run 1") {
+		t.Fatalf("second run: %v", texts(r))
+	}
+	r = call("3", `{"command":["sh","-c","echo fine"],"no_history":true}`)
+	if tx := texts(r); len(tx) != 2 || tx[1] != "exit status 0" {
+		t.Fatalf("no history: %v", tx)
+	}
+	r = call("4", `{"command":["no-such-command-abbreviatory"]}`)
+	if r["isError"] != true || !strings.Contains(texts(r)[0], "exit status 127") {
+		t.Fatalf("missing command: %v", r)
+	}
+	r = call("5", `{"command":["sh","-c","echo in $(pwd); cat"],"cwd":"`+dir+`","stdin":"from stdin\n","no_history":true}`)
+	if !strings.Contains(texts(r)[0], "in "+dir) || !strings.Contains(texts(r)[0], "from stdin") {
+		t.Fatalf("cwd and stdin: %v", texts(r))
+	}
+	start := time.Now()
+	r = call("6", `{"command":["sh","-c","echo started; sleep 30"],"timeout_seconds":1,"no_history":true}`)
+	if time.Since(start) > 10*time.Second || !strings.Contains(strings.Join(texts(r), "\n"), "time limit") {
+		t.Fatalf("timeout after %s: %v", time.Since(start), texts(r))
+	}
+	// A cancelled run is stopped and gets no answer; the next request does.
+	s.send(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"run","arguments":{"command":["sleep","30"],"no_history":true}}}`)
+	time.Sleep(300 * time.Millisecond)
+	start = time.Now()
+	s.send(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/cancelled","params":{"requestId":7}}`)
+	s.send(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":8,"method":"ping"}`)
+	if m := s.recv(); m["id"] != float64(8) {
+		t.Fatalf("after a cancel: %v", m)
+	}
+	// The default key is the directory and the command.
+	call("9", `{"command":["sh","-c","echo x ERROR a"],"cwd":"`+dir+`"}`)
+	s.send(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":10,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"history","arguments":{}}}`)
+	if h := texts(s.recv()["result"].(map[string]any))[0]; !strings.Contains(h, dir+": sh -c echo x ERROR a") || !strings.Contains(h, "job") {
+		t.Fatalf("history: %s", h)
+	}
+	s.in.Close()
+	select {
+	case <-s.done:
+	case <-time.After(15 * time.Second):
+		t.Fatal("the cancelled run wasn't stopped")
+	}
+	if time.Since(start) > 15*time.Second {
+		t.Fatal("cancelling took too long")
+	}
+}
+
+func buildBinary(t *testing.T) string {
+	bin := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "abbreviatory")
+	if out, err := exec.Command("go", "build", "-o", bin, ".").CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
+		t.Skipf("can't build: %v %s", err, out)
+	}
+	return bin
+}
+
+func execCommand(name string, args ...string) *exec.Cmd { return exec.Command(name, args...) }
+
+// Review of 0.3: batches and non-objects are invalid requests; a response
+// from the client gets no answer; the end of input stops running commands.
+func TestMCPMessagesAndShutdown(t *testing.T) {
+	s := startMCP(t, t.TempDir())
+	for _, msg := range []string{`[{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping"}]`, `42`, `"ping"`} {
+		s.send(msg)
+		if e, ok := s.recv()["error"].(map[string]any); !ok || e["code"] != float64(-32600) {
+			t.Fatalf("%s: not an invalid request", msg)
+		}
+	}
+	s.send(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":99,"result":{}}`)
+	s.send(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"ping"}`)
+	if m := s.recv(); m["id"] != float64(2) {
+		t.Fatalf("a client response was answered: %v", m)
+	}
+	if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
+		return
+	}
+	marker := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "still-running")
+	s.send(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"run","arguments":{"command":["sh","-c","sleep 30 & echo $! > ` + marker + `; wait"],"no_history":true}}}`)
+	time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond)
+	start := time.Now()
+	go io.Copy(io.Discard, s.out) // the stopped run is still answered
+	s.in.Close()
+	select {
+	case <-s.done:
+	case <-time.After(10 * time.Second):
+		t.Fatal("the server waited for the running command")
+	}
+	if d := time.Since(start); d > 7*time.Second {
+		t.Fatalf("stopping took %s", d)
+	}
+	pid, _ := os.ReadFile(marker)
+	if p := strings.TrimSpace(string(pid)); p != "" {
+		// The signal lands a moment later; a zombie left for init counts
+		// as gone.
+		alive := func() bool {
+			st, err := os.ReadFile("/proc/" + p + "/stat")
+			if err != nil {
+				return exec.Command("kill", "-0", p).Run() == nil
+			}
+			f := strings.Fields(string(st))
+			return len(f) > 2 && f[2] != "Z"
+		}
+		for i := 0; i < 30 && alive(); i++ {
+			time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)
+		}
+		if alive() {
+			exec.Command("kill", "-9", p).Run()
+			t.Fatalf("what the command started (pid %s) is still running", p)
+		}
+	}
+}

+const raceEnabled = false
diff --git a/cmd/abbreviatory/parity_test.go b/cmd/abbreviatory/parity_test.go

+package main
+
+// The 0.3 acceptance test: the command line, the HTTP service and the MCP
+// server give the same results on the whole corpus. Each front end gets a
+// store of its own; every fixture is reduced with several option sets,
+// every reference in every report is expanded, and run histories built
+// through each are compared.
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"encoding/json"
+	"io"
+	"net/http"
+	"net/http/httptest"
+	"net/url"
+	"os"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"reflect"
+	"regexp"
+	"sort"
+	"strconv"
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+)
+
+// option sets, as command line flags; the HTTP and MCP forms are derived.
+type optSet struct {
+	name     string
+	format   string
+	budget   int
+	preserve *string
+	keep     []string
+	noStore  bool
+}
+
+func strp(s string) *string { return &s }
+
+var optSets = []optSet{
+	{name: "defaults"},
+	{name: "small", budget: 1024},
+	{name: "failures and a keep rule", budget: 2048, preserve: strp("failures"), keep: []string{`queue depth=3[0-9]|test_parse`}},
+	{name: "read as a log", format: "logs", budget: 3000},
+	{name: "nothing preserved, no store", preserve: strp(""), noStore: true},
+}
+
+func (o optSet) flags() []string {
+	var f []string
+	if o.format != "" {
+		f = append(f, "-format", o.format)
+	}
+	if o.budget != 0 {
+		f = append(f, "-budget", strconv.Itoa(o.budget))
+	}
+	if o.preserve != nil {
+		f = append(f, "-preserve", *o.preserve)
+	}
+	for _, k := range o.keep {
+		f = append(f, "-keep", k)
+	}
+	if o.noStore {
+		f = append(f, "-no-store")
+	}
+	return f
+}
+
+func (o optSet) query() url.Values {
+	v := url.Values{}
+	if o.format != "" {
+		v.Set("format", o.format)
+	}
+	if o.budget != 0 {
+		v.Set("budget", strconv.Itoa(o.budget))
+	}
+	if o.preserve != nil {
+		v.Set("preserve", *o.preserve)
+	}
+	for _, k := range o.keep {
+		v.Add("keep", k)
+	}
+	if o.noStore {
+		v.Set("no_store", "true")
+	}
+	return v
+}
+
+func (o optSet) args() map[string]any {
+	a := map[string]any{}
+	if o.format != "" {
+		a["format"] = o.format
+	}
+	if o.budget != 0 {
+		a["budget"] = o.budget
+	}
+	if o.preserve != nil {
+		a["preserve"] = *o.preserve
+	}
+	if len(o.keep) > 0 {
+		a["keep"] = o.keep
+	}
+	if o.noStore {
+		a["no_store"] = true
+	}
+	return a
+}
+
+// frontEnds are the three ways in, each with its own store.
+type frontEnds struct {
+	t                   *testing.T
+	cliDir, mcpDir      string
+	srv                 *httptest.Server
+	mcp                 *mcpServer
+	token               string
+	cliRuns, mcpRunsOut bytes.Buffer
+}
+
+func newFrontEnds(t *testing.T) *frontEnds {
+	f := &frontEnds{t: t, cliDir: t.TempDir(), mcpDir: t.TempDir(), token: "s3cret"}
+	f.srv = httptest.NewServer(newHandler(core{t.TempDir()}, f.token, 1<<30))
+	t.Cleanup(f.srv.Close)
+	f.mcp = &mcpServer{c: core{f.mcpDir}, out: io.Discard, running: map[string]*mcpCall{}}
+	return f
+}
+
+func decode(t *testing.T, data []byte) map[string]any {
+	t.Helper()
+	var m map[string]any
+	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &m); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("not JSON: %v\n%s", err, data)
+	}
+	return m
+}
+
+// normal drops what may differ between front ends for good reason: the
+// time a run was recorded.
+func normal(v any) any {
+	switch x := v.(type) {
+	case map[string]any:
+		out := map[string]any{}
+		for k, val := range x {
+			if k != "time" {
+				out[k] = normal(val)
+			}
+		}
+		return out
+	case []any:
+		out := make([]any, len(x))
+		for i, val := range x {
+			out[i] = normal(val)
+		}
+		return out
+	}
+	return v
+}
+
+// jsonRound passes a value through JSON, so maps built in Go compare with
+// maps decoded from JSON.
+func jsonRound(t *testing.T, v any) any {
+	data, err := json.Marshal(v)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	var out any
+	json.Unmarshal(data, &out)
+	return out
+}
+
+func (f *frontEnds) cliReduce(path string, extra ...string) map[string]any {
+	args := append([]string{"reduce", "-store", f.cliDir, "-json"}, extra...)
+	args = append(args, path)
+	out, errs, code := runCLI(f.t, "", args...)
+	if code != 0 {
+		f.t.Fatalf("cli %v: exit %d: %s", args, code, errs)
+	}
+	return decode(f.t, []byte(out))
+}
+
+func (f *frontEnds) httpDo(method, path string, body io.Reader, accept string) (int, []byte) {
+	req, _ := http.NewRequest(method, f.srv.URL+path, body)
+	req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+f.token)
+	if accept != "" {
+		req.Header.Set("Accept", accept)
+	}
+	resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
+	if err != nil {
+		f.t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	defer resp.Body.Close()
+	data, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
+	return resp.StatusCode, data
+}
+
+func (f *frontEnds) httpReduce(path string, q url.Values) map[string]any {
+	file, err := os.Open(path)
+	if err != nil {
+		f.t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	defer file.Close()
+	code, data := f.httpDo("POST", "/reduce?"+q.Encode(), file, "")
+	if code != 200 {
+		f.t.Fatalf("http reduce %s: %d %s", q.Encode(), code, data)
+	}
+	return decode(f.t, data)
+}
+
+// mcpCall calls a tool and returns its result.
+func (f *frontEnds) mcpCall(name string, args map[string]any) map[string]any {
+	params, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{"name": name, "arguments": args})
+	res, rerr := f.mcp.call(params, nil)
+	if rerr != nil {
+		f.t.Fatalf("mcp %s: %v", name, rerr.Message)
+	}
+	return jsonRound(f.t, res).(map[string]any)
+}
+
+func mcpText(r map[string]any) string {
+	return r["content"].([]any)[0].(map[string]any)["text"].(string)
+}
+
+var anyRefRE = regexp.MustCompile(`(?:\[ref |"ref": "|, ref )([0-9a-f]{12})(?::([^\]"\s)]+))?`)
+
+func TestFrontEndsAgree(t *testing.T) {
+	paths, _ := filepath.Glob("../../test/fixtures/*")
+	var fixtures []string
+	for _, p := range paths {
+		if info, err := os.Stat(p); err == nil && info.Mode().IsRegular() {
+			fixtures = append(fixtures, p)
+		}
+	}
+	sort.Strings(fixtures)
+	if len(fixtures) < 8 {
+		t.Fatalf("expected the fixtures, found %d", len(fixtures))
+	}
+	sets := optSets
+	if testing.Short() || raceEnabled {
+		// The race detector makes this slow: the defaults and one other set
+		// still cover every fixture and every reference.
+		sets = optSets[:2]
+	}
+	f := newFrontEnds(t)
+	reductions, expansions := 0, 0
+	for _, path := range fixtures {
+		name := filepath.Base(path)
+		for _, o := range sets {
+			cli := f.cliReduce(path, o.flags()...)
+			web := f.httpReduce(path, o.query())
+			m := f.mcpCall("reduce", mergeArgs(o.args(), map[string]any{"path": path}))
+			if m["isError"] == true {
+				t.Fatalf("%s, %s: mcp: %s", name, o.name, mcpText(m))
+			}
+			viaMCP := m["structuredContent"].(map[string]any)
+			if !reflect.DeepEqual(cli, web) || !reflect.DeepEqual(cli, viaMCP) {
+				t.Fatalf("%s, %s: the front ends differ\ncli:  %v\nhttp: %v\nmcp:  %v", name, o.name, cli, web, viaMCP)
+			}
+			if mcpText(m) != cli["text"] {
+				t.Fatalf("%s, %s: mcp text differs from the report", name, o.name)
+			}
+			reductions++
+			if o.noStore {
+				continue
+			}
+			// Every reference expands to the same bytes everywhere.
+			text := cli["text"].(string)
+			refs := anyRefRE.FindAllStringSubmatch(text, -1)
+			if len(refs) == 0 {
+				t.Fatalf("%s, %s: no references in\n%s", name, o.name, text)
+			}
+			for _, r := range refs {
+				ref := r[1]
+				if r[2] != "" {
+					ref += ":" + r[2]
+				}
+				a, errs, code := runCLI(t, "", "expand", "-store", f.cliDir, ref)
+				if code != 0 {
+					t.Fatalf("cli expand %s: %s", ref, errs)
+				}
+				hc, b := f.httpDo("GET", "/expand/"+url.PathEscape(ref), nil, "")
+				if hc != 200 {
+					t.Fatalf("http expand %s: %d %s", ref, hc, b)
+				}
+				mc := f.mcpCall("expand", map[string]any{"ref": ref, "max_bytes": 64 << 20})
+				if mc["isError"] == true {
+					t.Fatalf("mcp expand %s: %s", ref, mcpText(mc))
+				}
+				if a != string(b) || a != mcpText(mc) {
+					t.Fatalf("%s: expand %s differs (%d, %d, %d bytes)", name, ref, len(a), len(b), len(mcpText(mc)))
+				}
+				expansions++
+			}
+		}
+	}
+
+	// Run histories: the same sequence of runs through each front end gives
+	// the same changes, run by run, and the same histories.
+	histories := 0
+	for _, path := range fixtures {
+		name := filepath.Base(path)
+		data, _ := os.ReadFile(path)
+		if (testing.Short() || raceEnabled) && len(data) > 1<<20 {
+			continue
+		}
+		other := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), name)
+		os.WriteFile(other, everyThirdLineDropped(data), 0o600)
+		key := "parity " + name
+		for i, p := range []string{path, other, other, path} {
+			cli := f.cliReduce(p, "-key", key, "-budget", "2048")
+			q := url.Values{"key": {key}, "budget": {"2048"}}
+			web := f.httpReduce(p, q)
+			m := f.mcpCall("reduce", map[string]any{"path": p, "key": key, "budget": 2048})
+			viaMCP := m["structuredContent"].(map[string]any)
+			if !reflect.DeepEqual(cli, web) || !reflect.DeepEqual(cli, viaMCP) {
+				t.Fatalf("%s, run %d: the front ends differ\ncli:  %v\nhttp: %v\nmcp:  %v", name, i+1, cli["delta"], web["delta"], viaMCP["delta"])
+			}
+		}
+		cliOut, _, _ := runCLI(t, "", "history", "-store", f.cliDir, "-json", key)
+		_, webOut := f.httpDo("GET", "/runs/"+url.PathEscape(key), nil, "")
+		m := f.mcpCall("history", map[string]any{"key": key})
+		a, b, c := normal(decode(t, []byte(cliOut))), normal(decode(t, webOut)), normal(m["structuredContent"])
+		if !reflect.DeepEqual(a, b) || !reflect.DeepEqual(a, c) {
+			t.Fatalf("%s: histories differ\ncli:  %v\nhttp: %v\nmcp:  %v", name, a, b, c)
+		}
+		histories++
+	}
+	var cliList, mcpList []any
+	out, _, _ := runCLI(t, "", "history", "-store", f.cliDir, "-json")
+	json.Unmarshal([]byte(out), &cliList)
+	_, webData := f.httpDo("GET", "/runs", nil, "")
+	var webList []any
+	json.Unmarshal(webData, &webList)
+	mcpList = f.mcpCall("history", map[string]any{})["structuredContent"].(map[string]any)["histories"].([]any)
+	// Listed most recent first; the front ends recorded in the same order.
+	if !reflect.DeepEqual(normal(cliList), normal(webList)) || !reflect.DeepEqual(normal(cliList), normal(mcpList)) {
+		t.Fatalf("history lists differ:\n%v\n%v\n%v", cliList, webList, mcpList)
+	}
+	t.Logf("%d fixtures: %d reductions, %d expansions and %d histories the same through the command line, HTTP and MCP", len(fixtures), reductions, expansions, histories)
+}
+
+func mergeArgs(a, b map[string]any) map[string]any {
+	for k, v := range b {
+		a[k] = v
+	}
+	return a
+}
+
+func everyThirdLineDropped(data []byte) []byte {
+	if bytes.HasPrefix(bytes.TrimSpace(data), []byte("{")) || bytes.HasPrefix(bytes.TrimSpace(data), []byte("<")) {
+		// A document: change one value instead of breaking it.
+		if bytes.Contains(data, []byte(`"error"`)) {
+			return bytes.Replace(data, []byte(`"error"`), []byte(`"Error"`), 1)
+		}
+		return bytes.Replace(data, []byte("<failure"), []byte("<skipped"), 1)
+	}
+	var out []byte
+	for i, l := range bytes.SplitAfter(data, []byte("\n")) {
+		if i%3 != 2 {
+			out = append(out, l...)
+		}
+	}
+	return out
+}
+
+// The report alone, as text, is the same through all three too.
+func TestFrontEndsAgreeOnText(t *testing.T) {
+	f := newFrontEnds(t)
+	path := "../../test/fixtures/gotest-json.txt"
+	cliText, _, _ := runCLI(t, "", "reduce", "-store", f.cliDir, path)
+	file, _ := os.Open(path)
+	defer file.Close()
+	_, webText := f.httpDo("POST", "/reduce", file, "text/plain")
+	mcp := mcpText(f.mcpCall("reduce", map[string]any{"path": path}))
+	if cliText != string(webText) || cliText != mcp {
+		t.Fatalf("texts differ:\n%s\n---\n%s\n---\n%s", cliText, webText, mcp)
+	}
+	data, _ := os.ReadFile(path)
+	if mcp2 := mcpText(f.mcpCall("reduce", map[string]any{"text": string(data)})); mcp2 != cliText {
+		t.Fatal("reducing text and reducing the file differ")
+	}
+	if !strings.Contains(cliText, "FAILED (7)") {
+		t.Fatalf("unexpected report:\n%s", cliText)
+	}
+}

+//go:build !windows
+
+package main
+
+import (
+	"os/exec"
+	"syscall"
+)
+
+// ownGroup starts the command in a process group of its own, so stopping it
+// stops what it started too.
+func ownGroup(cmd *exec.Cmd) {
+	cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true}
+}
+
+// stopGroup asks the command's process group to stop, or kills it.
+func stopGroup(cmd *exec.Cmd, kill bool) error {
+	sig := syscall.SIGTERM
+	if kill {
+		sig = syscall.SIGKILL
+	}
+	return syscall.Kill(-cmd.Process.Pid, sig)
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,20 @@
+//go:build windows
+
+package main
+
+import (
+	"os/exec"
+	"strconv"
+)
+
+// ownGroup does nothing on Windows; stopGroup stops the process tree instead.
+func ownGroup(cmd *exec.Cmd) {}
+
+// stopGroup ends the command and every process it started (taskkill /T),
+// or, if that fails, the command alone.
+func stopGroup(cmd *exec.Cmd, kill bool) error {
+	if err := exec.Command("taskkill", "/T", "/F", "/PID", strconv.Itoa(cmd.Process.Pid)).Run(); err != nil {
+		return cmd.Process.Kill()
+	}
+	return nil
+}

diff --git a/cmd/abbreviatory/serve.go b/cmd/abbreviatory/serve.go
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..f98d58d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/cmd/abbreviatory/serve.go

+package main
+
+// abbreviatory serve: the HTTP service. It answers on this machine only
+// unless a token is set, and then asks every caller for it.
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"crypto/subtle"
+	"errors"
+	"flag"
+	"fmt"
+	"io"
+	"net"
+	"net/http"
+	"net/url"
+	"os"
+	"os/signal"
+	"runtime"
+	"strconv"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+
+	abbreviatory "github.com/abbreviatory/engine"
+	"github.com/abbreviatory/engine/store"
+)
+
+// DefaultAddr is where serve listens unless told otherwise.
+const DefaultAddr = "127.0.0.1:7878"
+
+func cmdServe(args []string, stdout, stderr io.Writer) int {
+	fs := flag.NewFlagSet("serve", flag.ContinueOnError)
+	fs.SetOutput(stderr)
+	addr := fs.String("addr", DefaultAddr, "address to listen on")
+	token := fs.String("token", "", "require this bearer token (default $ABBREVIATORY_TOKEN); needed to listen beyond this machine")
+	dir := storeFlag(fs)
+	maxBody := fs.String("max-body", "1GB", "largest input accepted")
+	fs.Usage = func() {
+		fmt.Fprint(stderr, "Usage: abbreviatory serve [flags]\n\nServes reduce, expand and run histories over HTTP:\n  POST /reduce        the request body is the input; returns JSON (or the\n                      report alone with Accept: text/plain)\n  GET  /expand/{ref}  what a reference points to\n  GET  /runs          the histories; GET /runs/{key} one history's runs\n  GET  /healthz       {\"status\": \"ok\"}\n\n")
+		fs.PrintDefaults()
+	}
+	if err := fs.Parse(args); err != nil {
+		if errors.Is(err, flag.ErrHelp) {
+			return 0
+		}
+		return 2
+	}
+	if fs.NArg() > 0 {
+		fs.Usage()
+		return 2
+	}
+	if *token == "" {
+		*token = os.Getenv("ABBREVIATORY_TOKEN")
+	}
+	limit, err := parseSize(*maxBody)
+	if err != nil {
+		fmt.Fprintln(stderr, "abbreviatory: -max-body:", err)
+		return 2
+	}
+	if !isLoopback(*addr) && *token == "" {
+		fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "abbreviatory: %s is reachable from other machines; set -token (or $ABBREVIATORY_TOKEN) to serve there\n", *addr)
+		return 2
+	}
+	c := core{*dir}
+	if _, err := c.store(); err != nil {
+		fmt.Fprintln(stderr, "abbreviatory:", err)
+		return 1
+	}
+	ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", *addr)
+	if err != nil {
+		fmt.Fprintln(stderr, "abbreviatory:", err)
+		return 1
+	}
+	srv := &http.Server{
+		Handler:           newHandler(c, *token, limit),
+		ReadHeaderTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
+		// A body may be a large log on a slow link, but not forever.
+		ReadTimeout: 30 * time.Minute,
+		IdleTimeout: 2 * time.Minute,
+	}
+	fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "abbreviatory %s: serving on http://%s\n", abbreviatory.Version, ln.Addr())
+
+	stop := make(chan os.Signal, 1)
+	signal.Notify(stop, stopSignals...)
+	defer signal.Stop(stop)
+	done := make(chan error, 1)
+	go func() { done <- srv.Serve(ln) }()
+	select {
+	case err := <-done:
+		fmt.Fprintln(stderr, "abbreviatory:", err)
+		return 1
+	case <-stop:
+		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
+		defer cancel()
+		srv.Shutdown(ctx)
+		return 0
+	}
+}
+
+// isLoopback reports whether addr only listens on this machine.
+func isLoopback(addr string) bool {
+	host, _, err := net.SplitHostPort(addr)
+	if err != nil {
+		return false
+	}
+	if host == "localhost" {
+		return true
+	}
+	ip := net.ParseIP(host)
+	return ip != nil && ip.IsLoopback()
+}
+
+// newHandler is the HTTP API over c. With a token, every request but the
+// health check must carry it as "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN". Without one
+// the service is for this machine only, and it also turns away what a web
+// page in the user's browser could send it: a request for another host name
+// (DNS rebinding) or with a foreign Origin (a cross-site form or fetch).
+func newHandler(c core, token string, maxBody int64) http.Handler {
+	// Reductions take memory and CPU: a few at a time. A slot is only taken
+	// once the body has arrived, so a slow upload holds up nobody else.
+	// (Expansions stream and need no slot.)
+	heavy := make(chan struct{}, max(2, runtime.NumCPU()))
+	mux := http.NewServeMux()
+	mux.HandleFunc("GET /healthz", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+		replyJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"status": "ok", "version": abbreviatory.Version})
+	})
+	mux.HandleFunc("POST /reduce", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+		q, err := requestFromQuery(r)
+		if err != nil {
+			replyError(w, err)
+			return
+		}
+		body, err := spoolInput(http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxBody))
+		if err != nil {
+			replyError(w, err)
+			return
+		}
+		defer os.Remove(body.Name())
+		defer body.Close()
+		select {
+		case heavy <- struct{}{}:
+			defer func() { <-heavy }()
+		case <-r.Context().Done():
+			return
+		}
+		o, err := c.reduce(body, q, r.Context().Done())
+		if err != nil {
+			replyError(w, err)
+			return
+		}
+		if wantsText(r) {
+			for _, warn := range o.Warnings {
+				w.Header().Add("Abbreviatory-Warning", warn)
+			}
+			w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/plain; charset=utf-8")
+			io.WriteString(w, o.Res.Text)
+			return
+		}
+		replyJSON(w, http.StatusOK, o.JSON())
+	})
+	// {ref...}: a JSON pointer reference has slashes, encoded or not.
+	mux.HandleFunc("GET /expand/{ref...}", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+		lw := &lazyWriter{w: w}
+		if err := c.expand(lw, r.PathValue("ref")); err != nil && !lw.started {
+			replyError(w, err)
+			return
+		}
+		if !lw.started {
+			lw.start() // an empty part
+		}
+	})
+	runs := func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+		key := r.PathValue("key")
+		if key == "" {
+			all, err := c.histories()
+			if err != nil {
+				replyError(w, err)
+				return
+			}
+			if wantsText(r) {
+				w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/plain; charset=utf-8")
+				io.WriteString(w, historiesText(all))
+				return
+			}
+			replyJSON(w, http.StatusOK, historiesJSON(all))
+			return
+		}
+		h, err := c.history(key)
+		if err != nil {
+			replyError(w, err)
+			return
+		}
+		if wantsText(r) {
+			w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/plain; charset=utf-8")
+			io.WriteString(w, historyText(h))
+			return
+		}
+		replyJSON(w, http.StatusOK, historyJSON(h))
+	}
+	mux.HandleFunc("GET /runs", runs)
+	mux.HandleFunc("GET /runs/{key...}", runs)
+
+	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+		if token == "" {
+			if !loopbackHost(r.Host) {
+				replyJSON(w, http.StatusForbidden, map[string]any{"error": "this service answers for localhost only; set a token to serve other host names"})
+				return
+			}
+			if o := r.Header.Get("Origin"); o != "" && !loopbackOrigin(o) {
+				replyJSON(w, http.StatusForbidden, map[string]any{"error": "requests from web pages aren't accepted"})
+				return
+			}
+		} else if r.URL.Path != "/healthz" && !validBearer(r.Header.Get("Authorization"), token) {
+			w.Header().Set("WWW-Authenticate", `Bearer realm="abbreviatory"`)
+			replyJSON(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, map[string]any{"error": "a bearer token is required"})
+			return
+		}
+		mux.ServeHTTP(&jsonErrors{ResponseWriter: w}, r)
+	})
+}
+
+// validBearer checks an Authorization header; the scheme is case-insensitive.
+func validBearer(header, token string) bool {
+	scheme, got, ok := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(header), " ")
+	if !ok || !strings.EqualFold(scheme, "Bearer") {
+		return false
+	}
+	return subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(strings.TrimSpace(got)), []byte(token)) == 1
+}
+
+// loopbackHost reports whether a Host header names this machine.
+func loopbackHost(host string) bool {
+	h := host
+	if hh, _, err := net.SplitHostPort(host); err == nil {
+		h = hh
+	}
+	h = strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimPrefix(h, "["), "]")
+	if strings.EqualFold(h, "localhost") {
+		return true
+	}
+	ip := net.ParseIP(h)
+	return ip != nil && ip.IsLoopback()
+}
+
+// loopbackOrigin reports whether an Origin header is a page on this machine.
+func loopbackOrigin(origin string) bool {
+	u, err := url.Parse(origin)
+	return err == nil && (u.Scheme == "http" || u.Scheme == "https") && loopbackHost(u.Host)
+}
+
+// lazyWriter sets the headers for raw bytes on the first write, so an error
+// found before anything is written can still get its own status.
+type lazyWriter struct {
+	w       http.ResponseWriter
+	started bool
+}
+
+func (l *lazyWriter) start() {
+	l.started = true
+	l.w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/octet-stream")
+	l.w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
+}
+
+func (l *lazyWriter) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
+	if !l.started {
+		l.start()
+	}
+	return l.w.Write(p)
+}
+
+// jsonErrors turns the mux's own plain-text 404 and 405 answers into JSON,
+// as every other error is.
+type jsonErrors struct {
+	http.ResponseWriter
+	swallow bool
+}
+
+func (j *jsonErrors) WriteHeader(code int) {
+	if (code == http.StatusNotFound || code == http.StatusMethodNotAllowed) && strings.HasPrefix(j.Header().Get("Content-Type"), "text/plain") {
+		j.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
+		j.Header().Del("X-Content-Type-Options")
+		j.ResponseWriter.WriteHeader(code)
+		writeJSON(j.ResponseWriter, map[string]any{"error": http.StatusText(code)})
+		j.swallow = true
+		return
+	}
+	j.ResponseWriter.WriteHeader(code)
+}
+
+func (j *jsonErrors) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
+	if j.swallow {
+		return len(p), nil
+	}
+	return j.ResponseWriter.Write(p)
+}
+
+// requestFromQuery reads a reduction's options from the query string:
+// format, budget, preserve, keep (repeatable), key, full, no_store, command
+// and exit, as the command line's flags.
+func requestFromQuery(r *http.Request) (request, error) {
+	v := r.URL.Query()
+	q := request{Format: v.Get("format"), Keep: v["keep"], Key: v.Get("key"), Command: v.Get("command")}
+	if s := v.Get("budget"); s != "" {
+		n, err := strconv.Atoi(s)
+		if err != nil {
+			return q, usagef("budget: %q is not a number", s)
+		}
+		q.Budget = n
+	}
+	if v.Has("preserve") {
+		p := v.Get("preserve")
+		q.Preserve = &p
+	}
+	var err error
+	if q.Full, err = boolParam(v.Get("full")); err != nil {
+		return q, usagef("full: %v", err)
+	}
+	if q.NoStore, err = boolParam(v.Get("no_store")); err != nil {
+		return q, usagef("no_store: %v", err)
+	}
+	if s := v.Get("exit"); s != "" {
+		n, err := strconv.Atoi(s)
+		if err != nil {
+			return q, usagef("exit: %q is not a number", s)
+		}
+		q.Exit = &n
+	}
+	_, err = q.options()
+	return q, err
+}
+
+func boolParam(s string) (bool, error) {
+	if s == "" {
+		return false, nil
+	}
+	return strconv.ParseBool(s)
+}
+
+func wantsText(r *http.Request) bool {
+	a := r.Header.Get("Accept")
+	return strings.HasPrefix(a, "text/plain")
+}
+
+func replyJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, v any) {
+	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
+	w.WriteHeader(status)
+	writeJSON(w, v)
+}
+
+// replyError answers with the status that fits the error.
+func replyError(w http.ResponseWriter, err error) {
+	status := http.StatusInternalServerError
+	var ue *usageError
+	var be *abbreviatory.BudgetError
+	var mb *http.MaxBytesError
+	var ie *abbreviatory.InputError
+	switch {
+	case errors.As(err, &ue):
+		status = http.StatusBadRequest
+	case errors.As(err, &mb):
+		status = http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge
+	case errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound), errors.Is(err, errNoHistory):
+		status = http.StatusNotFound
+	case errors.As(err, &ie):
+		status = http.StatusBadRequest
+		if !strings.HasPrefix(ie.Msg, "JSON:") {
+			break
+		}
+		fallthrough
+	case errors.As(err, &be), errors.Is(err, abbreviatory.ErrBinary):
+		status = http.StatusUnprocessableEntity
+	}
+	replyJSON(w, status, map[string]any{"error": err.Error()})
+}
